key_insight: DrugHarness gives drug-discovery AI agents a flexible scientific toolkit and a mechanism for developing skills from execution histories and outcome feedback. It combines composable operations with adaptation to changing evidence and constraints.
problem_solved: Computational drug discovery requires agents to coordinate diverse scientific tools, track candidates and results, and adjust workflows as evidence and constraints change.
method: Integrate over 80 scientific operations, biomedical resources, and task-specific code into one execution environment.
Preserve associations among drug candidates, results, and generated artifacts throughout workflows.
Use execution trajectories and outcome feedback for conditional skill induction; the supplied abstract is truncated before further details.
impact: DrugHarness offers AI/ML practitioners a blueprint for building adaptable scientific agents with traceable workflows. The supplied excerpt does not include evaluation results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram linking an AI agent, the harness, scientific tools, and biomedical resources.
Feedback loop showing execution trajectories and outcomes feeding conditional skill induction.
Traceability graph connecting drug candidates to operations, results, and artifacts.
Workflow diagram illustrating adaptation when new evidence or constraints appear.
paper_title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
paper_authors: Yuxing Chen, Zhisheng Zhang, Cheng Tang, Wei Li, Minghui Zhang
